'''Daniel Eduardo Friedmann''' serves as Carbon Engineering's CEO and Board Chair. Friedmann assumed the role of CEO in January, 2022, having served on CE's board for the previous five years, four of which as Board Chair.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Carbon Engineering Ltd.|date=2022-01-10|title=Carbon Engineering Announces Leadership Transition|url=https://carbonengineering.com/news-updates/leadership-transition-2022/|access-date=2022-01-17|website=carbonengineering.com}}</ref>

Until 2016, Friedmann was CEO of [[MacDonald, Dettwiler and Associates]] for 20 years, during which time the company's revenue grew 19-fold and market capitalization increased 35-fold.<ref>{{Cite web|last=B. de Selding|first=Peter|date=April 22, 2016|title=Q&A {{!}} MDA Corp. CEO Friedmann steps down, saying company needs a U.S. citizen to grow|url=https://spacenews.com/qa-mda-corp-ceo-friedmann-steps-down-saying-company-needs-a-u-s-citizen-to-grow/|access-date=2022-01-17|website=spacenews.com}}</ref>

==Career==
Friedmann was born Sept. 19, 1956, in Chile, and immigrated to Vancouver as a teenager; his family was part of a group that left Chile during the [[presidency of Salvador Allende]].<ref name="GlobeEarth">{{cite news|last=Ebner|first=David|date=6 January 2012|title=MDA's Daniel Friedmann likes the Earth under his feet|work=[[The Globe and Mail]]|location=Toronto|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/careers/careers-leadership/mdas-daniel-friedmann-likes-the-earth-under-his-feet/article1358367/?page=all}}</ref><ref name=NP2012/> He studied [[engineering physics]] at the University of British Columbia and in 1979 went to work for [[MacDonald, Dettwiler and Associates]], a company that at that time specialized in hardware and software for satellite ground stations.<ref name=GlobeEarth/> Over time the company started to work on satellites, designing and eventually owning Canada's [[RADARSAT]] system, and around 1990 diversified into software for the real estate industry, buying BC OnLine from provincial government of British Columbia.<ref name=GlobeEarth/> Friedmann rose through the ranks and became president in 1993 and CEO in 1995.<ref name=GlobeEarth/>  As CEO he tried to focus the company on the real estate business and to exit the satellite business by selling it to a US company in 2008; the Canadian government vetoed the deal on national security grounds.<ref name=GlobeEarth/> Friedmann sold the real estate business in 2010 and focused MDA on developing businesses based on its engineering expertise, like robotics,<ref name=GlobeEarth/> and going deeper into the satellite business, buying the satellite builder, [[SSL (company)|SSL]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite news|last1=de Selding|first1=Peter B.|title=MDA's $1.1B Purchase of SS/L Seen as Boost for Both Firms|url=http://spacenews.com/mdas-11b-purchase-ssl-seen-boost-both-firms/|work=Space News|date=27 June 2012}}</ref>

Friedmann stepped down as CEO in 2016 to make way for an executive from the US.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Bouw|first1=Brenda|title=Satellite maker MDA's outgoing CEO looks back on 80 profitable quarters|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/rob-magazine/satellite-maker-mdas-outgoing-ceo-looks-back-on-80-profitable-quarters/article30520060/|date=June 27, 2016}}</ref>

Friedmann was selected as a 2015–2016 Brendan Wood TopGun CEO in Canada for Technology, Media and Telecommunications.<ref>{{cite news|title=Press Release: TopGun CEOs|url=http://topgunpress.com/brendan-wood-announces-topgun-ceos-in-canada-selected-by-shareholders/|work=Brendan Wood International|date=February 29, 2016}}</ref>

Friedmann is currently CEO and Chairman of [[Carbon Engineering]],<ref name=":0"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://carbonengineering.com/company-profile/|title=Carbon Engineering: Team and Board|publisher=}}</ref> a company dedicated to removing CO<sub>2</sub> from the air to aid in [[climate change mitigation|solving climate change]].

== Self-published books ==

He has published several books: ''The Genesis One Code'' in 2012, ''The Broken Gift'' in 2013. The books offered his beliefs about how the [[Tanakh]] can be reconciled with modern scientific understanding.<ref name=NP2012>Jane McDougall, [https://nationalpost.com/life/god-meets-science-in-a-new-book-the-two-get-along-quite-well "God meets science: In a new book, the two get along quite well"] , National Post, June 9th, 2012.</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Zerbisias|first1=Antonia|title=Ideacity: Has Daniel Friedmann found 'biblical clock' and key to creation?|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/insight/2013/06/14/ideacity_has_daniel_friedmann_found_biblical_clock_and_key_to_creation.html|work=Toronto Star|date=June 14, 2013}}</ref>
He also published ''Roadmap to the End of Days'' in 2017, ''The Biblical Clock'' in 2019,<ref>[https://readersfavorite.com/book-review/the-biblical-clock/ Readers Favorite Review of "The Biblical Clock"]</ref> ''Mysteries of the First Instant'' in 2021, and a business book ''An MBA from Heaven'' in 2019.<ref>[https://limmudvan20.sched.com/event/XgED/an-mba-from-heaven/ Limmud Vancouver 2020 presentation]</ref>
